brief: A file organizer as a spatial canvas — documents arranged by topic proximity, not lists or grids

dominant_strengths: Strong typographic hierarchy with crisp category labels and consistent meta line styling across every card
Colorful icon tiles create a recognizable file-type language that doubles as visual anchoring per cluster
Conceptually fresh take: spatial proximity instead of folder lists genuinely interprets the brief
dominant_weaknesses: Cluster overlap clips card titles (2024 OKRs Draft, Market Research Report) — proximity reads as collision, not meaning
No visible spatial logic: distance between clusters feels arbitrary, with empty quadrants and crowded ones unrelated to topic affinity
Floating untitled cards (Project Kickoff, Q3 Metrics, Meeting Action Items) have no parent group, breaking the topic-proximity premise
fix_priorities: Resolve z-index/overlap so cluster cards never occlude sibling content; add collision padding
Introduce explicit proximity cues — connecting lines, gravitational halos, or shared-color washes — so spatial meaning is legible
Assign every document to a visible cluster or render orphan items with a distinct 'unfiled' affordance
Add a minimap/zoom control (the bottom-right swatch hints at one) for navigation at canvas scale
rationale.norman_balance: Visceral curiosity from the canvas metaphor outpaces behavioral clarity, while reflective payoff suffers because overlaps undermine trust in the spatial system.
rationale.intent_fit: It commits to the spatial-canvas brief conceptually but fails to encode topic proximity as a readable, non-colliding spatial signal.
